decisions.reason: The revised definition selects an information statement delivered to a group, with speech and writing both included; the opening-hours example is unambiguous. Accept the proposed B2 as a conservative editorial course placement for this public-information noun, while retaining the literal Collins B1+ observation. Neither a conversion nor dictionary B2 certification is claimed.

The recipient-directed information definition and delivery-team example fit the selected communication noun. Retain A2 only as the course floor; the observed Oxford and Collins A1 labels remain literal. Program data packets and a literary central idea are separate senses.

The definition and an email example select one message. Oxford separates the countable message from the service, while Collins uses one A1 variable-noun entry with both. Retain A2 as the course floor without transferring the verb A2 label. Existing email spelling and general region remain exact.

The definition selects an actual telephone conversation, supported by the selected Oxford and Collins A1 evidence. Retain the A2 course floor and exact two-word form. Unanswered attempts and queued calls are not silently narrowed or approved by this sense.

The revised definition accurately selects a stored spoken message for later playback without requiring that every recording follow an unanswered call. Merriam-Webster 2b directly supports the countable message. Accept editorial B1 for familiar recorded-message handling, with no selected-source CEFR certification; system-only B1 evidence is not transferred.

The stored internal-number meaning is supported by numbered telephone-line definitions and examples. Accept editorial B2 for this bounded everyday office use, preserving the selected Collins B2 and Oxford C1 disagreement. Ext. remains an observation rather than an additional answer form.

The revised example clearly introduces two colleagues to one another and removes the introductory-talk ambiguity. Accept the unchanged people-acquaintance definition and editorial B1 for describing this social act. No level from a book opening or introductory course is transferred, and ambiguous expression bindings remain held.

Words or actions acknowledging an arriving person and the visitor example match the selected meeting sense. Accept the proposed B2 as a conservative editorial placement for the lexical noun in this course, with literal Collins B1+ retained. This is not a statement that greeting someone or saying hello requires B2 proficiency; written seasonal wishes remain separate.

Usually informal accurately qualifies the spoken-exchange definition without making informality mandatory. The schedule example fits and Collins labels the selected talk sense A2. Keep text-only and modality-uncertain contexts separate, without narrowing their existing broader meanings.

The topic-focused detailed conversation definition and delivery-problem example are clear. Oxford labels this selected exchange A2 and distinguishes a written treatment. No specialist conclusion, agreement or permission follows from lexical acceptance.
